tasks.title: Filter out zero-point leagues from expected wins and trends calculations
tasks.description: Bug: On /expected-wins/trends, user 'edgecdec' shows 2020 with 0% actual win rate and ~50% expected win rate. This is caused by a league where the user scored 0 total points (likely a test league or a league where the regular season never happened). The matchup data exists with 0-point entries, so totalOpportunities > 0 passes the current filter, and expected wins calculate to ~50% because ties with other 0-point teams count as 0.5. Fix: In src/services/stats/expectedWins.ts, after calculating a user's stats in analyzeLeague(), treat a team with 0 total pointsFor as having no valid data — return userStats as undefined so the league is excluded from aggregation. This fix will apply globally to all pages using analyzeLeague() (the main expected-wins page, trends, and league-history views). Verify by checking that 2020 no longer appears in the trends chart for edgecdec.

tasks.title: Add 50% average reference line to luck trends chart
tasks.description: On /expected-wins/trends, add a horizontal dashed line at 50% on the Y axis to indicate where the average player would be. Use Recharts ReferenceLine component with y={50}, a gray stroke, dashed strokeDasharray, and a label like 'Average'. This gives visual context for whether the user is performing above or below the league median over time.

tasks.title: Show Draft Assistant for edgecdec user instead of dev-only
tasks.description: In src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx, the Draft Assistant nav item is currently gated behind process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'. Change this so it is instead shown when the logged-in Sleeper user is 'edgecdec'. Use the existing useUser() hook to get the current user and check user.username === 'edgecdec'. The MENU_ITEMS list should be computed dynamically (e.g. via useMemo) rather than at module scope, since it now depends on runtime user state. Remove the NODE_ENV check entirely.

tasks.title: Ensure 50% reference line is always visible on luck trends chart
tasks.description: Bug: The 50% dashed reference line added in TASK-002 is not visible when all data points are above or below 50%, because the YAxis domain is set to auto and Recharts clips the chart to the data range. Fix: In src/app/expected-wins/trends/page.tsx, change the YAxis domain so it always includes 50. For example, use a domain function like domain={[dataMin => Math.min(dataMin, 48), dataMax => Math.max(dataMax, 52)]} to ensure the 50% line is always within the visible area with a small buffer. Do NOT hardcode 0-100 — the axis should still auto-scale to the data, just guaranteed to include the 50% mark.

tasks.title: Exclude already-rostered players from draft assistant in dynasty leagues
tasks.description: In dynasty leagues, most players are already rostered from previous seasons and are NOT in the draft pool — only rookies and free agents are draftable. Currently BestAvailable (src/components/draft/BestAvailable.tsx) only filters out players picked in the current draft via the picks array. Fix: When a draft is selected in src/app/draft-assistant/page.tsx, use the draft's league_id to fetch all rosters via SleeperService.getRosters(league_id). Collect every player_id from all rosters' 'players' arrays into a Set of rostered player IDs. Pass this Set (or array) as a new prop 'rosteredPlayerIds' to BestAvailable. In BestAvailable, filter out both drafted picks AND rostered players from the available pool. This should only apply when the league is a dynasty/keeper league — check the league settings (fetch the league via SleeperService.getLeague(league_id) and check if settings.type === 2 for dynasty, or if the draft has keeper picks). If it's a redraft league (type 0), skip the roster fetch since all players are available. Also display a small indicator in the UI (e.g. a Chip or subtitle) showing whether the draft is 'Dynasty' or 'Redraft' so the user knows the filtering is active.

tasks.title: Show traded pick ownership in draft assistant
tasks.description: In dynasty leagues, draft picks can be traded between owners. The Sleeper API provides GET /league/{league_id}/traded_picks which returns an array of objects with season, round, roster_id (original owner), owner_id (current owner after trade), and previous_owner_id. Similarly GET /draft/{draft_id}/traded_picks returns traded picks for a specific draft. When a draft is selected in the draft assistant, fetch the traded picks data and build a mapping of which roster_id actually owns each pick. Display this in the DraftBoard component — for each pick slot, show the actual owner (not just the original drafter). This is critical for dynasty leagues like 'Graham's Football Fantasy' where edgecdec has acquired extra picks via trades. The user should be able to see at a glance which picks they own across all rounds, including picks traded from other teams. Add a visual indicator (e.g. highlight or badge) on picks owned by the current user that were acquired via trade.

tasks.title: Add deterministic league-based URLs for draft assistant
tasks.description: Currently the draft assistant lives at /draft-assistant with no URL state — selecting a draft is ephemeral. Add a route /draft-assistant/[leagueId] that deep-links directly to a specific league's draft. When a user selects a draft from the list on /draft-assistant, navigate to /draft-assistant/{league_id}. The [leagueId] page should auto-fetch the league's drafts and select the most relevant one (active 'drafting' first, then 'pre_draft', then most recent 'complete'). This allows bookmarking and sharing direct links to a league's draft view. Create src/app/draft-assistant/[leagueId]/page.tsx as a new route. The existing /draft-assistant/page.tsx remains as the search/discovery page.

tasks.title: Display actual usernames instead of 'Team X' throughout draft assistant
tasks.description: Throughout the draft assistant (DraftBoard, traded pick labels, pick ownership displays), teams are shown as 'Team X' using roster_id numbers. Instead, fetch the league users via SleeperService (GET /league/{league_id}/users) and rosters to build a mapping of roster_id -> display_name. Use this mapping everywhere a team is referenced — in the DraftBoard column headers, in traded pick annotations like 'via trade → Team 10' (should be 'via trade → username'), and in any pick ownership display. Pass this mapping as a prop or compute it at the page level and pass down. REFERENCE: A previous Python/Flask implementation exists at https://github.com/edgecdec/SleeperLiveDraftRankingsV2 — clone it to /tmp/SleeperLiveDraftRankingsV2 and study src/backend/api/draft.py and src/backend/services/sleeper_api.py for how traded picks, team names, and draft order were handled. Port the relevant logic to TypeScript.

tasks.title: Support snake and third-round-reversal draft order in DraftBoard
tasks.description: The DraftBoard currently assumes linear draft order (same pick order every round). Sleeper drafts can be 'snake' (order reverses each round) or 'linear'. Some snake drafts also use third-round reversal (3rd round reverses again so the team picking last in round 1 picks first in round 2 AND first in round 3). The draft type is available in the SleeperDraft object's 'type' field ('snake' or 'linear') and third-round reversal may be in settings. Fix the DraftBoard to correctly calculate pick positions based on draft type: for snake drafts, reverse the column order on even rounds; for third-round reversal, the team with pick N in round 1 gets pick N in round 3 as well (rounds 3,5,7... follow round 1 order, rounds 2,4,6... are reversed). The pick_no from the actual picks data is the source of truth for completed picks — this is mainly needed for projecting upcoming pick slots in pre_draft or drafting states. REFERENCE: Clone https://github.com/edgecdec/SleeperLiveDraftRankingsV2 to /tmp/SleeperLiveDraftRankingsV2 and study src/backend/api/draft.py for the snake/reversal draft order logic. Port to TypeScript.

tasks.title: Add team focus/filter to draft board
tasks.description: Add a row of clickable team buttons at the top of the DraftBoard showing each team's username (from the roster_id -> username mapping in TASK-008). Clicking a team filters the draft board to only show that team's picks across all rounds, including picks acquired via trade (from TASK-006). Clicking the same team again or an 'All' button deselects the filter and shows the full board. When a team is focused, display their picks in a compact list view showing round, pick number, and the player selected (or 'TBD' if not yet picked). Highlight the focused team's username button with the primary color. This lets users quickly see a specific team's full draft capital at a glance. REFERENCE: Clone https://github.com/edgecdec/SleeperLiveDraftRankingsV2 to /tmp/SleeperLiveDraftRankingsV2 and study the frontend JS and draft API for any team filtering patterns.

tasks.title: Use DraftBoard column headers as team focus buttons instead of separate button row
tasks.description: TASK-010 added a separate row of team filter buttons above the DraftBoard. Remove that button row entirely. Instead, make the existing column headers in the DraftBoard table itself clickable — each column header already shows the team username, so clicking it should toggle focus on that team (same filtering behavior as TASK-010). Add a cursor pointer and hover effect to the column headers to indicate they are clickable. When a team is focused, highlight that column header with the primary color. Clicking the same header again deselects the filter. This is cleaner and avoids duplicating the team names in a separate ugly button row.

tasks.title: Separate mock drafts from real league drafts in draft list
tasks.description: On /draft-assistant, the draft list shows all drafts including mock drafts which clutter the view. Mock drafts are drafts whose league never became a real active league (no regular season games played, or the league status is 'pre_draft'/'drafting' with no matchup data). When fetching drafts in src/app/draft-assistant/page.tsx, for each draft use its league_id to check if the league actually had a real season — fetch the league via SleeperService and check if status is 'in_season' or 'complete', or if settings indicate it was a real league. Show real league drafts first in the list. Mock drafts should be collapsed into a separate section at the bottom labeled 'Mock Drafts' that is collapsed by default (use MUI Accordion or a show/hide toggle). This keeps the main list focused on drafts that matter.

tasks.title: Add football-themed maintenance page shown during deploys
tasks.description: Create a maintenance.html file in the project root that is shown by nginx when the app is down (during deploys/restarts). Follow the same pattern as MarchMadness: a simple standalone HTML page with inline CSS, no external dependencies. Use meta http-equiv refresh with content=10 to auto-retry every 10 seconds. Make it football-themed — use a 🏈 emoji as the icon, dark background (#121212), title 'Declanalytics', message like 'Halftime! We're making some updates.' with a subtitle 'This page will automatically refresh.' Keep it clean and minimal. Then SSH to the server and update the nginx config at /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/fantasyfootball.edgecdec.com to add: error_page 502 503 504 /maintenance.html; and location = /maintenance.html { root /var/www/FantasyFootball; internal; } — matching the pattern used by marchmadness.edgecdec.com. Run nginx -t and systemctl reload nginx to apply.

tasks.title: Add football emoji favicon to browser tab
tasks.description: Add a 🏈 football emoji as the browser tab favicon. The simplest approach is to add a SVG favicon in src/app/layout.tsx metadata using a data URI: <link rel='icon' href='data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22 viewBox=%220 0 100 100%22><text y=%22.9em%22 font-size=%2290%22>🏈</text></svg>'/>. Add this via the Next.js metadata icons field or as a direct link tag in the head. Remove or replace the existing favicon.ico if present.

tasks.title: Investigate and fix missing Graham's Football Fantasy 2025 draft
tasks.description: Bug: On /draft-assistant for user edgecdec, the actual 2025 Graham's Football Fantasy draft is missing from the list. The league ID is 1206336001794920448 (visible at https://sleeper.com/leagues/1206336001794920448/matchup). This league had many complicated trades. Investigate why this draft doesn't appear — possible causes: the draft may be associated with a different season year (dynasty leagues carry forward via previous_league_id chains, so the 2025 draft may be under a different league_id that is the current season's version of this league), or the getDrafts call may be filtering it out. Use the Sleeper API to trace the league chain: GET /league/1206336001794920448 to find the current season's league_id via previous_league_id links, then check its drafts. Fix the draft discovery logic so this draft appears. This is critical for verifying traded pick functionality.

tasks.title: Fix snake/3RR draft board player assignment — players mapped to wrong cells
tasks.description: Bug: In snake drafts, the DraftBoard displays the correct pick numbers per team column but assigns the WRONG players to cells. Example: draft 1268841650294099968 (PharmacyBX) — edgecdec picked Justin Jefferson (1st), Ashton Jeanty (2nd), Brock Bowers (3rd), Jayden Daniels (4th) but the board shows Drake London and George Kittle in the 2nd and 4th slots. The issue is that the pick-to-cell mapping is wrong: the code correctly calculates which pick NUMBER belongs in each cell for snake order, but when it looks up which player was taken at that pick, it's using the wrong index or mapping. The picks array from Sleeper is ordered by pick_no (1, 2, 3...). Each pick has pick_no, roster_id, and player_id. The fix: when placing picks into the grid, use pick_no (the global sequential pick number) to find the correct pick from the array, NOT the array index or some derived position. For each cell in the grid, calculate what pick_no that cell represents, then find the pick with that pick_no in the picks array and display that player. Verify against draft 1268841650294099968 on Sleeper to confirm correctness.

tasks.title: Add rainbow pulsing highlight to current user's picks on draft board
tasks.description: On the DraftBoard, highlight all picks belonging to the current user (matched via their roster_id) with a classic animated rainbow border/glow effect. Use a CSS @keyframes animation that cycles through rainbow colors on the border or box-shadow, with a smooth pulsing transition. Apply this to both already-picked cells (showing the player) and upcoming empty cells that belong to the user (including traded picks from TASK-006). This makes it instantly obvious which picks are yours across the entire board. Define the keyframes animation in a style tag or sx prop — do not create a separate CSS file. Keep the animation subtle enough to not be distracting but visible enough to spot at a glance.

tasks.title: Make Best Available panel collapsible on draft assistant page
tasks.description: The Best Available panel on the draft assistant page takes up a fixed 3-column (lg=3) grid slot on the right side, reducing space for the DraftBoard. Make it collapsible: add a toggle button (e.g. a chevron or arrow icon) that slides the panel in/out. When collapsed, the DraftBoard should expand to use the full width (lg=12). When expanded, revert to the current layout (lg=9 board + lg=3 panel). Store the collapsed state in local component state. On smaller screens (md and below), the panel already stacks below — this is mainly for medium-large screens where horizontal space is tight. Use a smooth CSS transition for the slide effect.

tasks.title: Fix DraftBoard to display picks in snake/3RR column order, not linear
tasks.description: Bug: The DraftBoard is displaying all picks in linear order (1.01, 2.01, 3.01 always in the leftmost column). In a snake draft, each user's picks should appear under THEIR column — e.g. if edgecdec has slot 3, his round 1 pick is in column 3, his round 2 pick is ALSO in column 3 (because snake reverses, so slot 3 in round 1 maps to slot N-2 in round 2 which snakes back to column 3). The pick cells must be placed in the column of the user who OWNS that pick (pre-trade), not in a fixed left-to-right sequential order. For each round, calculate which draft_slot picks in which position based on snake/3RR rules, then place the pick in that slot's column. The pick_no label (e.g. '2.10') should reflect the actual sequential pick number, but the CELL should be in the correct user's column. Verify against draft 1206336001803288576 on Sleeper.

tasks.title: Simplify traded pick label to arrow emoji and new owner username
tasks.description: On the DraftBoard, traded picks currently show 'via trade → AggressiveIyAvg' which is too verbose. Change the label to just show the ↔️ emoji followed by the new owner's username, e.g. '↔️ AggressiveIyAvg'. Remove the 'via trade →' text entirely. Keep it compact so it fits in the cell without wrapping.

tasks.title: Improve rainbow highlight to use a traveling gradient effect
tasks.description: The current rainbow highlight on the user's picks changes all cells to the same color simultaneously. Instead, use a CSS animated gradient border that slowly rotates/travels around each cell — so at any given moment, different parts of the border are different colors, and the colors smoothly shift position over time. This is the classic 'conic-gradient spinning border' effect. Implementation: use a conic-gradient background on a pseudo-element or wrapper with border-radius, animate the rotation with @keyframes. Each cell should have a slightly different animation-delay so they don't all pulse in sync — use the pick index to offset the delay. The animation should be slow and smooth (around 3-4 second full cycle), not fast or flashy.

tasks.title: Change team focus to fade other teams instead of hiding them
tasks.description: When clicking a team column header to focus on them, the current behavior changes the board layout entirely (hiding or restructuring other teams). Instead, keep the full board layout exactly the same but fade all non-focused team picks to ~10% opacity. The focused team's picks remain at full opacity. This preserves the board structure so you can still see context while the focused team's picks pop out visually. Apply the opacity transition with a smooth CSS transition (e.g. 0.3s ease). When no team is focused (clicking the same header again to deselect), all picks return to full opacity.

tasks.title: Progressively render positional benchmarks data as each league loads
tasks.description: On /performance/positional, the page currently waits until ALL leagues are processed before showing any data. Instead, update the UI progressively after each league finishes processing — render the charts/tables with whatever data is available so far, and update them as more leagues complete. Show a loading indicator at the top (e.g. LinearProgress bar with a text label like 'Loading league 3 of 8...') that remains visible until all leagues are done. Once complete, replace the loading indicator with a subtle 'All leagues loaded' confirmation or just remove it. The key change is in the page component's data fetching logic: instead of awaiting all results and then setting state once, set state incrementally after each league resolves so React re-renders with partial data.

tasks.title: Show position column in full list view on positional benchmarks page
tasks.description: Bug: On /performance/positional, when expanding to the full list view, the player's position (QB, RB, WR, TE, etc.) is not displayed as a column. Add a Position column to the full list table so users can see each player's position. This should be one of the first columns (after rank/name).

tasks.title: Add larger page size options (up to 1000) on positional benchmarks full list
tasks.description: On /performance/positional, the full list view pagination only offers small page sizes (10, 25, etc.). Add larger options so the rows per page selector includes 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, and 1000. This lets users view the entire list without excessive pagination. Update the rowsPerPageOptions prop on the MUI TablePagination (or equivalent pagination component) used in this view.

tasks.title: Rebuild positional history page with all-time season data
tasks.description: On /performance/positional/history, show all-time Portfolio MVPs and LVPs — not just the current season. Currently the positional benchmarks page only shows MVPs (most valuable players) and LVPs (least valuable players) for the current season. The history page should aggregate this data across ALL seasons (back to 2017) so users can see which players they've relied on the most (or been burned by the most) over their entire fantasy career. Fetch each season's leagues and positional data, accumulate player impact stats across all years, and rank them to produce all-time MVP and LVP lists. Show the number of seasons/leagues each player appeared in and their cumulative impact. Load progressively as each season completes (same pattern as TASK-024).

tasks.title: Add league-average comparison to historical positional efficiency
tasks.description: On /performance/positional/history, show the user's positional efficiency numbers compared to league averages for each season — the same way the current season page does it. For each season and each position (QB, RB, WR, TE), calculate the user's average points scored vs the league average at that position across all their leagues. Display this as a comparison (e.g. user avg vs league avg, or a +/- differential) so users can see which positions they outperformed or underperformed at relative to their competition over time. Ideally show this as a chart or table with seasons on one axis and positions on the other, with color coding (green for above average, red for below). This lets users identify multi-year trends like 'I've consistently been weak at TE' or 'My RBs carried me in 2022-2023'.

tasks.title: Add link to view draft on Sleeper from draft assistant page
tasks.description: On the draft assistant page (/draft-assistant/[leagueId]), add a link/button that opens the draft on Sleeper's website. The URL format is https://sleeper.com/draft/nfl/{draft_id}. Place it in the draft header bar (the Paper with the draft name and status) — an icon button or small text link like 'View on Sleeper' with an external link icon (OpenInNew from MUI icons). Opens in a new tab.

tasks.title: Fix draft board not fully visible — allow horizontal scroll and full-width layout
tasks.description: Bug: On /draft-assistant/[leagueId], the full draft board is not visible — columns are cut off and the user can't see all teams. The DraftGrid currently uses gridTemplateColumns with minmax(120px, 1fr) and minWidth of teams*130, which forces horizontal scrolling even when the user zooms out. Fix: remove the minWidth constraint and reduce the column minimum so the grid can shrink to fit the viewport. Use something like minmax(80px, 1fr) so that when zoomed out the entire board fits on screen without scrolling. The cells should use text truncation (noWrap + ellipsis) to handle narrow columns gracefully. The Container wrapping the draft page should also use maxWidth={false} or 'xl' to give maximum available width. The goal is: at normal zoom you see as much as fits with horizontal scroll available, but if you zoom out the whole board fits on one screen.

tasks.title: Apply zero-point league filtering across all pages in the application
tasks.description: In TASK-001, we fixed the expected-wins trends page to ignore leagues where the user scored 0 total points (test leagues or seasons that never happened). This same filtering needs to be applied everywhere in the application that processes league data across seasons. Audit ALL pages and services that iterate over a user's leagues: /performance/positional, /performance/positional/history, /performance, /portfolio, /portfolio/trends, /medic, /league-history, and any service functions that aggregate across leagues. Wherever a league's data is processed for a user, check if the user's total points scored is 0 and skip that league. The fix in TASK-001 was done in src/services/stats/expectedWins.ts by returning userStats as undefined when pointsFor is 0 — apply the same principle in other services (positionalBenchmarks.ts, leagueHistory.ts, etc.) or create a shared utility function like shouldSkipUserInLeague(pointsFor) that all services can use. Verify by checking that edgecdec's 2020 data does not appear on any page.

tasks.title: Fix zero-point filtering on /performance/positional/history — 2020 still showing
tasks.description: Bug: TASK-028 was supposed to apply zero-point league filtering globally but /performance/positional/history still shows 2020 for edgecdec, which should be excluded (user had 0 points that year — test league with no real games). Find the specific code path that fetches and aggregates data for the positional history page and add the zero-point check there. The page likely has its own data fetching loop that was missed by TASK-028. Check if it uses positionalBenchmarks.ts or has inline fetching. Wherever the user's points are summed per season, skip any league where the user's total points scored is 0. Verify edgecdec's 2020 no longer appears on this page after the fix.

tasks.title: Create trade fetching and parsing service for redraft leagues
tasks.description: Create src/services/stats/tradeAnalyzer.ts with a function to fetch all trades for a redraft league. Use the Sleeper API GET /league/{league_id}/transactions/{week} for each regular season week. Filter to only type='trade' transactions. Parse each trade into a structured format: trade id, week number, timestamp, and two sides — each side is an array of { roster_id, players: [player_id[]], draft_picks: [] }. Ignore draft pick trades for now (redraft focus). Also fetch league users and rosters to map roster_ids to usernames. Cache results per league. Export a TradeData type and a fetchLeagueTrades(leagueId, season) function.

tasks.title: Build per-player post-trade positional efficiency calculator
tasks.description: Add a function evaluateTradeEfficiency() to src/services/stats/tradeAnalyzer.ts. For each trade, for each player on both sides: fetch weekly matchup data for every week AFTER the trade through end of regular season. For each week the player was in the new team's starting lineup (starters array in matchup data), get their points scored. Calculate the league average points at that player's position for the same week (average across all starters at that position in the league that week). The player's efficiency for that week = their points minus the league positional average. Sum this across all started weeks to get total efficiency gained/lost. Return per-trade results with: each side's players, each player's total efficiency sum, per-week efficiency breakdown, weeks started count, and the overall side totals. A positive total means that side of the trade outperformed league average at those positions.

tasks.title: Create Trade Evaluator page under league history
tasks.description: Create a new page at src/app/league-history/[leagueId]/trades/page.tsx that shows all trades in a redraft league evaluated by positional efficiency. The page should be accessible from the league history view. For each trade, display: the week it happened, both sides with usernames, and for each player show their position, total efficiency +/- (sum across all started weeks after trade), weeks started, and per-week average efficiency. Color code positive efficiency green and negative red. Show a trade verdict summary comparing the total efficiency of each side. Sort trades by week (most recent first). Include a link back to the league history page. Load data progressively — show each trade's evaluation as it completes. Add a nav link or button from the existing /league-history page to access this trades view for each league.

tasks.title: Audit and add sortable columns to all existing data tables
tasks.description: Audit every data table across the application and ensure all applicable columns are sortable via clickable column headers using MUI TableSortLabel. Pages to check: /players (player database), /expected-wins (standings tables), /performance (season review tables), /performance/positional (benchmark tables and full list), /portfolio (ownership tables), /league-history (head-to-head and record tables), /medic (alert tables), and the trade evaluator. For each table, add sort state (sortBy, sortDirection) and a click handler on each column header that toggles sort. Numeric columns (points, wins, percentages, efficiency) and text columns (name, position, team) should all be sortable. Skip columns where sorting doesn't make sense (action buttons, icons). Use a consistent pattern — extract a shared sorting utility if the same sort logic is repeated across multiple tables.

tasks.title: Show draft picks and FAAB in trades with N/A for efficiency fields
tasks.description: On /league-history/[leagueId]/trades, trades involving draft picks or FAAB budget show as empty or 'No trackable players'. Instead, display draft picks (e.g. '2026 Round 1 Pick') and FAAB amounts (e.g. '$15 FAAB') as line items on the appropriate side of the trade, with N/A for efficiency, weeks started, and per-week average columns. The Sleeper transaction object has draft_picks array (with season, round, roster_id, owner_id) and waiver_budget array for FAAB. Parse these and display them alongside any real players in the trade. Only hide a trade entirely if BOTH sides have zero players AND zero picks AND zero FAAB — which shouldn't happen for a real trade. Additionally, if the draft for that season has already happened, resolve what the pick actually became — use the draft picks data (GET /draft/{draft_id}/picks) to find which player was selected with that pick and display it, e.g. '2025 Round 1 Pick → 1.03: Justin Jefferson'. This connects the pick to its outcome.

tasks.title: Limit trade efficiency window to actual tenure on team
tasks.description: The trade efficiency calculator currently counts all weeks from the trade through end of season for each player. If a player was traded away or dropped before the season ended, we'd be counting weeks they weren't on the team. Fix: only count weeks where the player actually appeared in the receiving team's starters array in the matchup data. This naturally handles re-trades — if a player was flipped in a later trade, they simply won't be in the starters after that week, so those weeks won't count. The value from flipping them is captured in the evaluation of that subsequent trade. No need to build a full transaction timeline — just check the matchup starters data which we already fetch. Additionally, if a player stopped appearing in starters before the season ended (indicating they were re-traded or dropped), display an asterisk (*) next to their name in the trade evaluator UI. On hover (MUI Tooltip), show a note like 'Re-traded in Week X' or 'Dropped in Week X' — determine the last week they appeared in starters and add 1 to get the approximate departure week.

tasks.title: Ensure only real trades are shown — filter out waivers and commissioner moves
tasks.description: On /league-history/[leagueId]/trades, verify that the trade fetching service only includes actual trades. Sleeper transactions have a 'type' field — only include type='trade'. Filter out 'waiver', 'free_agent', and 'commissioner' types. Also filter out any transaction with status != 'complete' to exclude failed or vetoed trades. Log the raw transaction types being fetched to confirm no non-trade transactions are leaking through.

tasks.title: Sort trades by impact on the trade evaluator page
tasks.description: On /league-history/[leagueId]/trades, default sort trades by absolute efficiency impact (largest difference between the two sides first) rather than by week. Add a sort toggle so users can switch between 'Most Impactful' (default) and 'Chronological' (by week). Impact is calculated as the absolute value of the difference between side A's total efficiency and side B's total efficiency — bigger gap means more lopsided trade.

tasks.title: URGENT: Fix crash on trade evaluator page — draftPicks is undefined
tasks.description: Bug: /league-history/1206336001794920448/trades crashes with 'TypeError: can't access property map, D.draftPicks is undefined'. The code is calling .map() on a draftPicks property that doesn't exist on some transaction objects. tasks.title: Create draft efficiency calculation service
tasks.description: Create src/services/stats/draftEfficiency.ts with a function calculateDraftEfficiency(leagueId, draftId, season). For every player picked in the draft: (1) Fetch weekly matchup data for all regular season weeks. (2) For each week, find the player in ANY team's starters array (not just the team that drafted them — if they were traded, still count their production). (3) Calculate the league average points at that player's position for that week (average across all starters at that position league-wide). (4) Player's weekly efficiency = their points minus the positional league average. (5) Sum across all weeks started to get total efficiency. (6) Track which team(s) the player was on (note if they changed teams mid-season). Return an array of DraftPickEfficiency objects: { pickNumber, round, draftSlot, playerId, playerName, position, team, totalEfficiency, weeksStarted, avgEfficiencyPerWeek, draftedByRosterId, draftedByUsername, changedTeams: boolean }. Also compute a logarithmic best-fit curve across all picks: expectedEfficiency = a * ln(pickNumber) + b, using least squares regression on the pick data. Return the curve coefficients alongside the pick data.
